scope: Add an opt-in conditioning tie-break over exact already-admissible route candidates and independently reconstruct actual completed n-mediated compensation episodes from the native journal plus accepted route-policy evidence. This sub-batch measures DCNH n-pair occupancy but does not declare stabilization, run the FT6 matched held-out/changed grid, or assign a subtype; those remain FT6.3.

source_contract.continuation_plan: Full Theory Engine Batched Plan revision 1.1, FT6.2
source_contract.accepted_predecessor: FT6.1 bounded paid-use history accepted; its scores were behaviorally inert
source_contract.geometry: hle.development_structure.portage and hle_unified.axes remain read-only; n is the value flip and its four unordered seat pairs are the inherited DCNH axis pairs

candidate_feedback.candidate_schema: Each candidate names one actor-owned prospective request, stable identity, TD5 priority class, exact estimated native time, exact extra energy, and the nonempty ordered native element sequence that the candidate predicts it will actually process.
candidate_feedback.admission: Ineligible candidates are discarded before comparison. A choice requires at least one eligible candidate and an exact FT6.1 checkpoint for the same actor and declared policy.
candidate_feedback.comparison: Minimize TD5 priority class, then estimated native time, then extra energy. Among candidates tied on all three pre-feedback coordinates, success-v1 and success-decay-v1 maximize the sum of current scores on the candidate's ordered actual elements. Null or feedback-off assigns zero feedback. Stable identity is the final deterministic tie-break.
candidate_feedback.priority_amendment: This prospectively registers the TD6 amendment permitted by TD5: feedback is inserted only after eligibility, priority class and both exact cost coordinates, but before stable identity. It cannot promote a worse class or cost, create access, make an option affordable, or change route eligibility.
candidate_feedback.causal_binding: A claimed behavioral effect must bind the chosen request to a later completed existing route-policy traversal. The exact committed paid element delta reconstructed from the raw native journal must equal the candidate's declared element multiset; a label or chooser record alone is insufficient.

compensation_episodes.source: Only a completed IntegratedRoutePolicy attempt whose selected mean is n and whose traversal reports actual content processing can propose an episode.
compensation_episodes.native_payment: For each actor/request, the episode window begins at the first route-policy event's raw journal index and ends at its completed traversal. The inherited completed-use observer must reconstruct a positive committed paid element delta over that exact window.
compensation_episodes.geometry: The traversal target must equal portage(origin_seat, 'n'). Its unordered origin/target pair must equal exactly one inherited AXES pair. The episode's DCNH cell is axis_cells(actor_tim) at that pair's inherited axis index.
compensation_episodes.occupancy: The latest completed episodes are a bounded sequence. For the latest six, measured occupancy is unique only when one DCNH cell occurs at least four times and no other cell ties its count. Otherwise occupancy is an explicit tie/insufficient result.
compensation_episodes.boundary: An occupancy result is measurement only. FT6.2 does not call it stabilized, does not apply the six-demand held-out persistence criterion, does not use the 2+1 formula, and does not assign a participant subtype.

invariants: Feedback never changes TIM, seat dimensionality, native law, reserve, certificate scope, route eligibility, affordability or any sealed predecessor source.
History scores originate only in the accepted FT6.1 paid-use accounting; candidate declarations cannot mint or alter scores.
Feedback cannot select outside the best eligible TD5 priority/cost equivalence class. Stable identity remains deterministic after feedback.
Every recorded compensation episode contains actual repeated n geometry and a positive paid committed native processing delta; counters alone never establish compensation.
DCNH labels are derived from the inherited n-pair geometry for the actor's immutable TIM. Ties remain ties.
The new modules are opt-in and change no default or accepted FT4/FT5/FT6.1 source.
gate: Thirteen exact FT6.2 methods pass with zero failures/errors; non-null history changes a later request choice only inside an exact eligible priority/cost tie; feedback-off and history-removal controls eliminate that difference; completed chosen work matches its declared paid native elements; repeated real n route traversals yield independently reconstructed paid DCNH-pair episodes; unique four-of-six occupancy and ties reconstruct exactly; all FT6.1-and-earlier method identities remain exact; frozen source is unchanged.
next: FT6.3 matched three-policy histories, six-demand held-out and six changed-demand schedules, history-removal, feedback-off and fixed-bias controls, plus the parent stabilization gate
theory_boundary: Passing is a bounded engineering feedback and occupancy hypothesis. It does not validate psychology, establish the 2+1 formula, elect a subtype, close TD6/TD7 or alter any C/D register.
